content: Vendor docs (NVIDIA WinOF-2) confirm advanced NIC driver parameters are not all present by default in the registry -- some must be manually created to override default behavior, and available value names/ranges differ per NIC vendor and driver version. Any 'tweak' UI that assumes a fixed value name exists across all adapters/drivers is unsafe; UI must enumerate the adapter's actual driver registry subkey (Class GUID + index) and only expose parameters that exist for that specific driver.
